notes: This opening describes the implemented work, not the original proposal. The 19 series are the 11 earlier rolling comparisons plus eight new player-study variants, all sharing the same four-year evaluation population. The first-study SVM/MLP are preserved in the 2025 account comparison but lack the same earlier rolling history. Strategies are combinations of model, selection, prices and stakes; 116 does not mean 116 different algorithms. There are no claimed executed real-money trades.

elements.text: Other acquired sources are preserved in the data inventory; this deck describes the inputs actually used in the models.

notes: The new loader reconciles whole-league historical player records to exact fixture sides; the historical membership is not a present-day roster assignment. Each season contains 20 clubs and 380 native fixtures. Current 2026/27 records are used only for lagged future features, never model fitting. Historical opposition is retained so relegated teams are not mislabeled as current clubs. The current snapshot contains 668 player summaries and 70 completed fixtures. Some historical role metadata are season-fixed proxies with unverified publication times.

notes: H/D/A denotes home win, draw and away win. Most value rules choose the maximum p×decimal-odds−1 above a fixed threshold, with deterministic H/D/A ties. Same-date requests use opening cash and are allocated before outcomes settle. Flat, cash-fraction and capped Kelly requests are distinct strategy configurations. This explains why the strongest probability model need not generate the largest account.

title: A chronological comparison on the same fixtures
subtitle: 1,470 quoted matches in four evaluation seasons. Historical redesigns remain exploratory.

elements.text: Fit preprocessing only on permitted fitting data. Freeze coefficients and calibration within each evaluation season.
Every comparable model sees the same evaluation fixtures. Earlier games may update later lagged inputs.
Repeatedly inspected history is not a new untouched test. The current-club cohort also creates selection limitations.

notes: Tune one of three fixed regularization or tree-leaf settings on the earlier tuning season, refit on training plus tuning, and fit one scalar temperature on the separate calibration season. No evaluation outcomes enter that fold's fit. The cohort comprises matches involving at least one saved current 2026/27 club, rather than every historical EPL fixture. A chronological boundary protects a fit, but cannot erase the fact these historical results have already been examined.

title: The strongest learned predictor still trails the market
subtitle: Observed pooled probability scores on the same 1,470 fixtures; lower log loss and Brier are better.

elements.text: Best learned = market residual with team data and seven FPL aggregates.
It uses bookmaker probabilities as an input. Its small historical changes do not establish incremental value over the market.

notes: Best means minimum observed pooled log loss among the 16 learned predictors with comparable four-year records. There are 19 series when the three baselines are included. Raw normalized inverse Bet365 odds are the strongest benchmark: log loss .96616994. The best learned model is the earlier team+player market-residual variant: .96929380. Its paired descriptive interval versus the raw market includes zero; there is no fresh or multiplicity-adjusted superiority result. ECE is classwise calibration error at ten bins and does not measure forecast resolution.

title: Best learned predictor: market residual + team/FPL
subtitle: 28 historical inputs + bookmaker-probability offset; regularized home/draw adjustments, then temperature calibration.

elements.text: WHAT THE MODEL DOES

Start from normalized inverse Bet365 odds.
Learn regularized adjustments from team form and seven rolling FPL aggregates.
Keep training, tuning and calibration chronological.
TRADING WRAPPER S029 | CONTINUOUS FOUR SEASONS
The raw market has lower pooled log loss (0.9662). S029's positive archived return is not proof of a validated predictive edge.

notes:
Starts with normalized inverse Bet365 odds and learns regularized H/D log-odds adjustments relative to away. Uses 28 historical inputs: 9 team performance, 4 context flags, 8 source-coverage controls and 7 rolling FPL aggregates. Separately temperature-calibrated. Uses odds as an input; is not an odds-free model.

The raw market has lower pooled log loss (0.9662). S029's positive archived return is not proof of a validated predictive edge.
The trading result is separate from probability quality. S029 takes the maximum model-implied edge above 5%, with flat requested stakes of 1,000, best archived quotes and date-start cash allocation. Hit ratio is a fraction of bets won. Classification accuracy is a fraction of all match outcomes correctly classified. All comparisons are retrospective. Full per-trade expected components and actual payoffs appear in the common-scope scorecard and workbook.

notes: The richer player squad block has 222 inputs, including fixed 1-GK/4-DEF/4-MID/2-FWD selections based on prior minutes. The combined block has 235. All six player-based variants have worse pooled log loss than their newly fitted same-algorithm team control. The primary population is unchanged; a better-supported-history sensitivity does not reverse the pooled ranking. This result concerns these particular representations and models, not a general claim that player information has no value. The 32 new rules include the matched team controls as well as player models.

title: Highest four-season ending capital: S060
subtitle: A historical capital leader, selected descriptively after comparing the 88 compatible accounts.

elements.text:
Market-residual model with team, xG and FPL inputs.
Choose maximum edge above 5%.
Quarter Kelly; 2% per-bet cap.
10% date-level cash budget; best archived quotes.
Its recorded ROI confidence interval crosses zero. The historical ranking does not select a validated live policy.

notes: S060 uses the combined market-residual probability series, which is not the best pooled probability-score variant. It adds xG to team and legacy FPL aggregates and uses Bet365 market probabilities as an offset. The strategy changes both staking and total date exposure relative to flat stake variants. Its positive capital result is an observed path, conditional on archived best quotes, and is not a multiplicity-adjusted discovery. A conditional date-bootstrap ROI interval crosses zero and does not include full model-refitting or strategy-selection uncertainty.

title: A one-season winner can fail over four seasons
subtitle: P028: team + full player block, logistic regression, Bet365 reference prices, quarter Kelly capped at 2% per bet.

elements.text: The model's pooled accuracy is 50.95% and log loss is 1.0161. A profitable slice does not establish better forecasting.

notes: P028 is the highest ending 2025/26 account among all 116, including the old strategies. Its continuous account contains the same 2025 season after three prior seasons and begins only once at 100000; it does not reset at the start of 2025. Its annual diagnostic starts a separate account at 100000 and must not be spliced into the continuous path. The underlying logistic model uses 235 inputs. All new player-study continuous paths lose, even though eight new-study paths are positive in 2025 alone. This is a concrete reason to show both time horizons.

title: The same-scope trading scorecard
subtitle: All rows: continuous four seasons, 1,470 priced opportunities, one initial 100,000 account.

elements.text:
Expected gain/loss use the model's probabilities and the recorded stakes. They are not average realized wins/losses.
Full observed payoffs, uncertainty and all 116 / 88 account metrics are in the companion workbook.

notes: The scorecard intentionally aligns all six featured policies to the same four-season scope. Expected gain per trade averages p times stake times odds minus one; expected loss averages one minus p times stake. These may look favorable even when actual trading loses because they rely on the model's probabilities, especially on selected high-edge bets. ROI divides net profit by turnover and is not return on starting capital. Frequency divides actual placed bets by all 1470 common priced opportunities; bankruptcy can reduce realized frequency. The companion workbook also preserves average observed winning/losing payoffs and the confidence intervals.

title: Historical profit depends on prices and path assumptions
subtitle: S060 illustrates why a quote replay and a payout-only repricing answer different questions.

elements.text:
Best quotes may come from different books.
Capture clocks and availability are unverified.
No stake limits or observed transaction costs are modeled.

Selections and sizing react to odds.
Cash exposure changes the later path.
Whole-date bootstrap intervals do not remove model or strategy selection uncertainty.
These archived-price paths do not demonstrate executable fills, arbitrage or prospective investment returns.

notes: Do not interpret the three displayed profits as a pure causal price effect. The full Bet365 replay computes model edge and requests again, so choices, bet count and cash sizes can differ. Fixed-exposure repricing keeps original selections and stakes and is a shadow comparison; some such paths in the wider study are unfunded, with normal capital and risk metrics withheld. This slide reports its profit only. Quote-time uncertainty also prevents a verified closing-line-value claim. No new fee scenario or outcome-based filter is chosen here.

subtitle: All money values are generic monetary units. Cash accounts have no deposits or borrowing.

Net profit / turnover; net profit / initial 100,000

notes: Expected components use the selected model probability at the recorded allocated stake. They are unconditional components per trade, not the conditional mean payoff of wins or losses. No-trade conditional quantities remain undefined in the source workbook. Log loss is negative mean log probability assigned to the observed H/D/A outcome; Brier is the unscaled three-class squared error. ECE is classwise calibration error, bin-dependent and descriptive. Cash stays flat when no interest is modeled. Conditional date-bootstrap intervals are not a full model-and-search uncertainty analysis.
